# Zoning Analysis: 1256 N Artesian Ave, Chicago, IL
**PIN: 16012280240000 | West Town (Community Area 24)**

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3 (Residential Single-Unit – Detached House)**, per the City of Chicago's official GIS zoning layer. You can verify this on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

The RS-3 district is described in [5]: its primary purpose is to accommodate detached houses on individual lots, differentiated from RS-1 and RS-2 primarily by minimum lot area requirements and floor area ratios.

---

## 2. Is a 3+ Unit Multi-Unit Residential Building Permitted by Right?

**No.** A building with 3 or more dwelling units is **not permitted by right** in RS-3. As described in [5], RS districts are intended for detached houses; RT districts accommodate two-flats and low-density multi-unit buildings; higher-density RM districts accommodate larger multi-unit buildings. In RS-3, the base zoning allows a **detached house (1 unit)**, and the density exemption in [1] permits at most a **two-unit building** under specific conditions (see §4 below). Three or more units would require rezoning to at least an RT or RM district.

---

## 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

The applicable standards are set out in [1] (§ 17-2-0300). I can state the following with confidence from the retrieved code sections:

**Minimum Lot Area per Dwelling Unit (RS-3):**
- The standard RS-3 minimum lot area per unit applies per [1].
- A **reduced minimum of 1,500 sq ft per unit** is available for a two-unit building when 60% or more of zoning lots fronting the same side of the street between the two nearest intersecting streets have been lawfully improved with multi-unit buildings — *or* when the property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries (§ 17-7-0591). At 3,150 sq ft, your lot would support at most **2 units** under this exemption [1].

**What I could not determine from the retrieved code:**
- The exact **standard** (non-reduced) minimum lot area per unit for RS-3, the **maximum FAR**, **maximum building height**, and **specific setback requirements** were not included in the retrieved Municipal Code chunks. These figures appear in §§ 17-2-0303 (density table), 17-2-0400 (floor area ratios), 17-2-0500 (height), and 17-2-0600 (setbacks/yards), which were not returned in this query. **You should consult those sections directly** in the [Chicago Municipal Code](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago_zoning_ordinanceamendments.html) or contact the Chicago Department of Planning and Development (DPD) for a formal zoning determination.

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

The following apply to this parcel:

- **Special District:** This parcel is within a Special District overlay. The specific nature and restrictions of this special district were not further described in the available data — you should confirm with DPD what regulations attach to it.

- **ADU Eligible Area:** This parcel falls within an **Additional Dwelling Unit (ADU)-Allowed RS Area** [2]. This means you may be eligible to add a **conversion unit** (within the principal building) and/or a **coach house** (accessory structure) in addition to the principal unit, subject to limitations set out in [2] (§ 17-7-0570) and enforced by the Department of Housing at pre-certification [2]. Coach house rules are governed by [4]: a coach house in an RS district requires compliance with § 17-7-0570 [4]; it may not exceed **22 feet in height** [4]; at least 3 feet of unobstructed open space must be provided between the coach house and at least one side property line [4].

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** This parcel is in an ARO zone. This is primarily triggered for residential developments of 10+ units or receiving city financial assistance — at the scale of a 1–2 unit RS-3 development it is unlikely to be triggered, but it is worth confirming with DPD. West Town's community area already has 20 ARO-related housing projects totaling 291 affordable units on record.

- **No Planned Development:** This parcel is not in a Planned Development.
- **No Landmark or Historic District:** Not in a landmark district, not a landmark building, not in a historic district, not on the National Register.
- **No Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) overlay:** The parcel is **not TOD-eligible** under the Connected Communities Ordinance, despite being 0.68 miles from the **Damen Blue Line** CTA station and 1.04 miles from the **Western Ave Metra (Milwaukee North)** station. TOD density/parking bonuses therefore do not apply.
- **No Special Service Area (SSA).**
- **No Lakefront Protection, PMD, or Planned Development overlays.**
- **Flood Zone X (Minimal Flood Hazard):** FEMA designation is Zone X — not a Special Flood Hazard Area. Flood insurance is not federally required.
- **No brownfield sites nearby.**

---

## 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reduction

Off-street parking in RS districts is regulated by [3]:

- Required parking spaces for residential uses **must be located on the same zoning lot** as the dwelling units served [3].
- Off-street parking is **prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line**, except when accessed by a permitted driveway from the front [3].

**Specific parking ratios** (spaces per unit) for RS-3 were not included in the retrieved code. They appear in § 17-10-0200 (parking quantity schedule), which was not returned. You should consult that section directly.

**Transit-related reduction:** The parcel is **not in a TOD overlay area**, so the automatic parking reductions available under the Connected Communities Ordinance do not apply by right. The Damen Blue Line is 0.68 miles away — walkable, but outside the TOD threshold. No transit-related parking reduction was confirmed from the available code sections.

**Coach house exception:** Notably, [4] specifies that coach houses may be established **without accessory parking** to serve the coach house unit itself, and required parking for the principal building on the same lot may be reduced or waived via administrative adjustment (§ 17-13-1003-OO) [4].

---

## 6. Maximum Units by Right — Can You Build 6 Units?

**Maximum by right: 1 unit (detached house), potentially 2 units under the block-predominance exemption, plus potentially 1–2 ADU units.**

Here is the breakdown:

| Path | Units | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Base RS-3 by right | **1** (detached house) | Always available |
| Two-unit exemption | **2** | If 60%+ of block-face lots are improved with multi-unit buildings, or "Predominance of Block" applies [1] |
| ADU conversion unit | **+1** | If ADU area rules allow, per [2] |
| ADU coach house | **+1** | If RS lot meets § 17-7-0570 requirements [2][4] |
| **Realistic maximum by right** | **~3–4** | Principal 2-flat + conversion + coach house, all subject to conditions |

**Can you build 6 units? No — not by right in RS-3.** Six units would require rezoning to an RM district (at minimum RM-4.5 or higher, depending on lot size and unit mix), which is a discretionary process requiring aldermanic support and DPD approval. The 3,150 sq ft lot is also quite small — even if rezoned, the minimum lot area per unit requirements of higher RM districts may limit achievable density.
